negatives.failure_signature: An unbounded recursive text scan across the large repository exceeded its sixty-second execution window.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The query combined a broad root with many historical documents instead of a Git-indexed or phase-bounded surface.
negatives.recovery: Switched to Git-indexed searches, exact filenames, and bounded phase directories.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Prefer git grep, rg --files followed by a bounded file set, or direct schema reads before any historical recursive content scan.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the timed-out scan produced no completeness evidence

negatives.failure_signature: The package manager could not remove one locked obsolete temporary executable directory after installing the requested CLI version.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The running desktop process held the old executable while the global package update completed.
negatives.recovery: Verified the new CLI version directly and left the locked temporary directory untouched for the operating system or a later nonrunning-process cleanup.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Treat post-install cleanup warnings separately from version verification; never delete an in-use executable tree during an active desktop session.
negatives.promotion_effect: CLI version verification passed; cleanup completeness remains unclaimed

negatives.failure_signature: The batch assumed a legacy proposal-ledger filename that the predecessor phase did not contain, causing the aggregate read to fail.
negatives.trigger_precondition: A filename was inferred from an older phase instead of discovered from the current predecessor tree.
negatives.recovery: Enumerated the exact predecessor phase files first and read the current x1-proposals filename.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use file discovery or manifest lookup before batched reads across evolving artifact schemas.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the failed batch produced no validation evidence

negatives.failure_signature: The first summary queried generic count fields and treated a missing records array as a populated base.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The query assumed a flattened index while the current artifact uses inherited_index plus new_records.
negatives.recovery: Inspected the schema property names and recursively decoded the inherited pointer chain.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Schema-introspect before field selection and validate effective_record_count against recursively collected unique IDs.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; only the corrected 270-record reconstruction is evidence

negatives.failure_signature: The first summary looked for a sources array, but the current ledger stores inherited_ledger plus added_sources.
negatives.trigger_precondition: A generic field name was assumed without reading the current ledger schema.
negatives.recovery: Read property names, then recursively combined added_sources through the inherited ledger chain.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use the declared schema and recursive pointer fields rather than guessed collection names.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; only the corrected source reconstruction is counted

negatives.failure_signature: A completed command was queried through an unavailable continuation surface and then through an already-closed completion token.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The caller did not first distinguish active asynchronous execution from a completed result.
negatives.recovery: Reverified the desired Git state directly from the repository and live remote.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use continuation polling only for an explicitly active command; otherwise re-read the authoritative state directly.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; exact four-way Git equality came from the direct verification

negatives.failure_signature: The first slate re-added four exact inherited authority URLs for secure development, credential status, accessibility, and cluster-randomized reporting.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The candidate slate was compared against remembered titles before recursively decoding all 186 inherited source rows.
negatives.recovery: Reused inherited source IDs V8-S22, V8-S12, V8-S26, and V6423-S41 and removed the duplicate additions before x1 freeze.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Run exact normalized-title and canonical-URL deduplication against the full inherited pointer chain before writing a source ledger.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the rejected duplicate rows are not counted in the v644-v5 source addition

negatives.failure_signature: The suite passed 616 of 617 tests; the inherited exact legacy constraint-hash alias returned true from CRLF worktree bytes before emitting its required retained-negative warning.
negatives.trigger_precondition: Automatic worktree line-ending conversion made the raw file hash equal the declared legacy hash, bypassing the exact alias-warning branch.
negatives.recovery: Re-materialized that unchanged inherited JSON file byte-for-byte with LF endings matching its Git blob and reran the complete suite.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Before the full suite, compare this named legacy fixture's raw hash with its immutable LF Git-blob hash and normalize only when the worktree conversion is the known cause.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the 616/617 run is retained failed evidence and only the later 617/617 run is promoted

negatives.failure_signature: A two-step line edit and reversion produced mixed line endings, yielding a third hash that matched neither the declared nor exact legacy alias.
negatives.trigger_precondition: A small patch rewrote only the touched line while preserving converted endings on untouched lines.
negatives.recovery: Recreated the complete small JSON file through the patch tool from its exact HEAD content, producing the expected LF byte hash and passing both isolated alias tests.
negatives.recurrence_guard: For an exact byte-level fixture, rematerialize the complete file from verified repository content rather than patching one line to induce normalization.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the mixed-ending file and failed isolated run are retained but not promoted

retention_rule: Recovery does not erase failure evidence; only successful corrected runs may be promoted.
